NKE.rationale: Nike is in a severe fundamental deterioration with no credible near-term catalyst to reverse the trajectory. The company's Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with revenue essentially flat at $11.28B. Operating income collapsed to $650M from $844M YoY, and operating cash flow plunged 76% to $430M. The Q4 FY2026 results (June 30, 2026) showed revenue down 1% to $10.97B, with a 12% decline in Greater China. The only reason EPS appeared to beat was a $986M one-time tariff refund; excluding that,, EPS was was $0.20, barely above the $0.14 a year ago. Gross margin excluding the tariff benefit was down 10bps. The company guideded 'flattish' earnings for the next two quarters with low-to-mid-single-digit revenue declines expected in Q1 FY2027. Valuation remains expensive at 29x P/E despite this fundamentalamental deterioration—down from 38x in early 2026 but still well above the 22-25x range seen in mid-2025. The stock has declined 6% from its 52-week high of $80.17, yet the market is still paying a premium for a business with shrinking margins, declining China sales, and no evidence of a sustainable turnaround. News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.278 over 90 days), and there is active speculation about Nike being removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average due to its low share price and weak performance. The new CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy is in early stages with no concrete evidence of success—wholesale recovery is offset by DTC declines, and the company admits it is 'not living up to our full potential.' All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating fundamentals, still-rich valuation, and no near-term catalyst for re-rating.
